practice.q: Which device normally forwards a frame inside one VLAN using a MAC address table?
practice.why: A Layer 2 switch keeps a local directory of MAC addresses and ports. It learns where senders are heard, then uses the receiver's destination MAC to choose the outgoing port within that VLAN.

practice.q: Which architecture connects every leaf switch to every spine switch?
practice.why: In spine–leaf, every leaf has a connection to every spine. A server on one leaf can normally reach a server on another through one spine, giving a predictable path pattern.

practice.q: Which medium is generally preferred for a long-distance optical link?
practice.why: Single-mode fiber is designed for longer optical distances with compatible long-reach transceivers. The cable and both end devices must support the same optical standard; the connector fitting is not enough.

practice.q: A port shows many CRC errors. What should you investigate first?
practice.why: A CRC error means a received Ethernet frame failed its corruption check. Start with cable/optical integrity and compatible link settings at both ends, then see whether new errors still appear.

practice.q: Which function is supplied by TCP but not by UDP itself?
practice.why: TCP numbers the bytes it sends, checks acknowledgments and resends missing data. These mechanisms provide ordered, reliable delivery. UDP itself does not provide them, although an application can add similar checks.

practice.q: What is the network address of 192.168.10.77/26?
practice.why: 1. A /26 leaves 32 − 26 = 6 host bits. 2. That gives 2^6 = 64 addresses per block. 3. The last-number blocks are 0–63, 64–127, 128–191 and 192–255. 77 belongs to 64–127, so the network is 192.168.10.64.

practice.q: Which address is in an RFC 1918 private range?
practice.why: The private block 172.16.0.0/12 includes second-number values 16 through 31. Because 20 is in that interval, 172.20.1.1 belongs to the private range. Not every address beginning with 172 is private.

practice.q: Which is a valid compression of 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001?
practice.why: Remove unnecessary zeros at the start of each four-digit group: 0db8 becomes db8 and 0001 becomes 1. Replace the consecutive all-zero groups with one ::. The result is 2001:db8::1; only one :: is allowed per address.

practice.q: Which prefix identifies IPv6 link-local unicast addresses?
practice.why: fe80::/10 marks IPv6 link-local addresses. They work only on their local link, so routers do not forward them to another link. A device with several interfaces may also need the outgoing interface named.

practice.q: A client reaches 1.1.1.1 but cannot resolve example.com. What should be checked next?
practice.why: Reaching a remote IP address shows that an IP path works for that test. Looking up a name is DNS's separate job, so check the configured DNS servers, their reachability and their answers next.

practice.q: Which 2.4 GHz channel set is commonly nonoverlapping with 20 MHz channels?
practice.why: For common 20 MHz 2.4 GHz networks, channels 1, 6 and 11 do not overlap one another in many regions. This helps neighboring access points reuse radio spectrum; legal channels and the local environment still matter.

practice.q: What does a VRF isolate?
practice.why: A VRF is a separate IP route list inside one routing device. Interfaces in different VRFs do not automatically route between one another just because they share the same hardware.

practice.q: Which field does a switch use to learn its dynamic MAC table?
practice.why: When a frame arrives, the switch reads its source MAC and remembers the arrival port and VLAN. That is learning. It later uses the destination MAC to decide where to deliver a frame.

practice.q: Two hosts in different VLANs need which function to communicate?
practice.why: VLANs create separate local Ethernet groups. A switch can deliver within one group, but moving an IP packet between their different subnets requires routing and usable gateways. Access rules can then limit that routed communication.

practice.q: What happens to native-VLAN traffic on a default 802.1Q Cisco trunk?
practice.why: On a typical Cisco 802.1Q trunk, frames belonging to its native VLAN travel without a VLAN tag by default. Both ends must agree which VLAN that untagged traffic belongs to. Explicit native-tagging support can change this behavior.

practice.q: Which discovery protocol is vendor neutral?
practice.why: LLDP is the multi-vendor discovery standard defined by IEEE 802.1AB. CDP is Cisco's own discovery protocol. Both describe directly connected neighbors rather than proving an entire application path works.

practice.q: Which LACP pairing forms a bundle?
practice.why: LACP active starts the bundle negotiation and passive responds. Active/passive can therefore form a bundle if the other link settings agree. Passive/passive leaves both sides waiting for someone else to start.

practice.q: Which device becomes the STP root bridge?
practice.why: Spanning Tree chooses the lowest bridge ID as its root reference. The configured priority is compared before the remaining identifying fields, so a lower priority value is preferred; the MAC address can break a later tie.

practice.q: Which AP mode supports local switching at a branch?
practice.why: FlexConnect can put a branch client's traffic directly onto the branch's local wired VLAN. That avoids sending that locally switched data across the WAN to the controller, provided the intended branch settings and services exist.

practice.q: An SSID works at Layer 2 but clients get no address. Which service path should be checked?
practice.why: The wireless connection can succeed while address assignment fails. Trace the client's VLAN to a working DHCP server or its configured relay, and check that the server has the correct address pool and a return path.

practice.q: Which protocol encrypts a remote CLI session?
practice.why: SSH encrypts the remote text-command session and supports identity checks. It protects the session in transit; a reachable management address, correct user authentication and suitable permissions are still separate requirements.

practice.q: A WLAN is configured but its SSID is not advertised. Which setting should be checked first?
practice.why: A WLAN can exist in configuration while being turned off administratively. Check that it and the required related objects are enabled and assigned to the intended AP before expecting the network name to appear.

practice.q: In [110/20] on an OSPF route, what is 110?
practice.why: IOS writes the two bracketed values as [administrative distance/metric]. In [110/20], 110 ranks this route source against other sources for the same prefix; 20 is OSPF's own path cost.

practice.q: A packet matches installed /16 and /24 routes. Which route is used?
practice.why: Both routes match, but /24 fixes more destination bits than /16 and covers a smaller address block. The router uses that more specific installed match. Administrative distance does not override it during this packet lookup.

practice.q: What makes a static route a floating backup?
options: An AD higher than the primary route
practice.why: A floating route has a higher administrative distance than the preferred route for the same destination block. It stays less preferred while the primary is available and can become usable after the primary route disappears.

practice.q: On a broadcast OSPF segment, which router is preferred as DR?
options: Highest priority, then highest router ID
practice.why: At a broadcast-segment election, eligible routers compare interface priority first and router ID second, preferring higher values. Priority 0 is ineligible. A later better candidate does not automatically replace an already elected DR.

practice.q: What address should clients normally use with an FHRP?
practice.why: Clients use the shared virtual gateway IP. The physical router serving that identity can change after a detected failure, so clients do not need to replace their gateway setting with the other router's real address.

practice.q: Which NAT type creates a fixed one-to-one address mapping?
practice.why: Static NAT pairs one chosen internal address with one fixed translated address. Unlike a dynamic pool assignment, the mapping is configured explicitly and does not wait to choose a free address from a pool.

practice.q: Which UDP port does NTP use?
practice.why: NTP uses UDP port 123 for time synchronization. This is an application port number, not a physical socket on the device. Synchronization still needs a suitable reachable source.

practice.q: Which DNS record stores an IPv6 address?
practice.why: An AAAA record stores an IPv6 address for a name. An A record stores an IPv4 address. DNS has separate record types because a name can have different kinds of information.

practice.q: Which SNMPv3 level includes authentication and encryption?
practice.why: In authPriv, auth means messages are authenticated and Priv means their content has privacy through encryption. authNoPriv supplies authentication without that encrypted-content protection.

practice.q: With logging trap warnings, which severity is included?
practice.why: Warnings is severity 4. The threshold includes its own level and all more serious lower numbers: 0 through 4. Error is 3, so it is included; informational 6 and debugging 7 are not.

practice.q: Where is ip helper-address configured for a client subnet?
practice.why: Put the helper on the routed gateway interface receiving the clients' local DHCP broadcasts. That interface can forward the request to the remote server and identify the client subnet. An ordinary Layer 2 access port does not perform that relay job.

practice.q: Which mechanism buffers traffic to smooth it to a configured rate?
practice.why: Shaping holds excess packets in a queue and sends them later at the intended rate. That smooths bursts but can add waiting time. Policing instead normally drops or relabels excess traffic rather than buffering it for later.

practice.q: Which VTY command restricts incoming sessions to SSH?
practice.why: transport input ssh restricts the configured VTY remote terminal lines to SSH transport and excludes Telnet from that list. It does not by itself create users, generate server keys or select the login database.

practice.q: Which statement about TFTP is correct?
practice.why: TFTP has no built-in username authentication or encryption. It is a simple UDP-based transfer protocol. A successful transfer therefore does not establish who was allowed to read it or that its contents were private.

practice.q: An unpatched software flaw is best described as what?
practice.why: A vulnerability is a weakness, such as an unpatched software defect. A threat could exploit that weakness; the weakness alone does not prove that an attack has already succeeded.

practice.q: Which behavior best addresses a suspicious request for credentials?
options: Verify through a trusted independent channel
practice.why: Use contact details you already know are legitimate to verify the request, then follow reporting procedures. Replying to the suspicious caller or using contact details they supplied does not provide independent verification.

practice.q: Which statement about service password-encryption is correct?
options: It is a substitute for strong secrets
It provides reversible obfuscation for certain passwords
practice.why: The legacy feature disguises some stored passwords using a reversible format. Someone can undo that encoding, so it should not be treated as strong secret protection or as encryption for a management session.

practice.q: Which pair represents different authentication factors?
practice.why: A password proves knowledge of a secret. A physical security key proves possession of a separate item. These are different factor categories; two passwords or a password plus PIN remain knowledge factors.

practice.q: Which VPN model connects two office networks through gateways?
practice.why: A site-to-site VPN joins office networks through their gateways. A remote-access VPN instead connects an individual endpoint, such as a traveling employee's laptop, to an organization.

practice.q: What happens if a packet matches no entry in an applied ACL?
practice.why: An applied ACL is checked from top to bottom. If no written entry matches, the packet reaches the unstated final deny and is blocked. Required traffic therefore needs a matching allowance before that point.

practice.q: Which control helps block rogue DHCP server replies on access ports?
practice.why: DHCP snooping filters server replies arriving through untrusted client-facing paths. Only deliberately trusted server/relay paths should deliver legitimate server messages; it can also build a table of observed client assignments.

practice.q: Which AAA function determines whether a user may execute a command?
practice.why: Authorization decides whether an identified user may perform an action. Authentication checks identity, while accounting records activity. A successful login does not automatically permit every command.

practice.q: Which mechanism is associated with WPA3-Personal?
practice.why: WPA3-Personal uses SAE, Simultaneous Authentication of Equals, for its password-based key exchange. It is intended to improve resistance to offline password guessing; strong credentials and correct configuration still matter.

practice.q: Which combination is appropriate for WPA2-Personal?
practice.why: WPA2-Personal uses a pre-shared key, or PSK, with AES-CCMP data protection. Enterprise 802.1X is a different authentication choice, even when the data-protection cipher is also AES-CCMP.

practice.q: What does idempotence mean in configuration automation?
options: Repeated application converges without unnecessary changes
practice.why: An idempotent desired-state action leaves the intended state stable when repeated. For example, ensuring a hostname is R1 should not keep making new changes once it is R1. Arbitrary repeated shell commands do not automatically behave this way.

practice.q: What is a key controller-based networking benefit?
practice.why: A controller can coordinate policy and administration across many devices. Those devices still forward traffic and run software; centralized coordination does not mean every user packet must pass through the controller.

practice.q: Which plane performs packet forwarding?
practice.why: The data plane is the part that forwards packets using installed forwarding information. The control plane learns or calculates that information, and the management plane supports administration and observation.

practice.q: Which is an example of predictive AI in network operations?
practice.why: Forecasting congestion estimates a future condition, so it is predictive AI. Producing a new summary or configuration draft is generative AI. Either output still needs comparison with actual evidence.

practice.q: Which HTTP method generally makes a partial resource update?
practice.why: PATCH requests a partial change to a resource. PUT generally supplies a replacement representation. Use the API's documented format and permissions; neither method name alone proves the resulting network works.

practice.q: Which Terraform operation previews proposed infrastructure changes?
practice.why: terraform plan previews proposed changes by comparing configuration, stored state and observed resources. It is a preview step; terraform apply performs the changes as a separate operation.

practice.q: What data type is the value of "interfaces" in {"interfaces":["Gi0/0","Gi0/1"]}?
practice.why: Square brackets identify an array, an ordered list. Here interfaces contains two text strings, Gi0/0 and Gi0/1. Braces would identify an object of named key/value pairs instead.

practice.q: How many traditionally usable host addresses does a /27 provide?
practice.why: A /27 leaves 32 − 27 = 5 host bits. 2^5 gives 32 total addresses. On an ordinary IPv4 subnet, subtract the network and broadcast addresses: 32 − 2 = 30 usable host addresses.

practice.q: What is the broadcast address of 10.0.0.130/25?
practice.why: A /25 has 128 addresses per block. Last-number ranges are 0–127 and 128–255. 130 belongs to the second block, whose final address is 10.0.0.255; that final address is its broadcast.

practice.q: Which mask corresponds to /28?
practice.why: /28 uses 24 network bits in the first three numbers and four in the last. Those last four positions have weights 128, 64, 32 and 16. Their sum is 240, so the mask is 255.255.255.240.

practice.q: Which flags establish a TCP connection?
practice.why: The TCP client starts with SYN. The server answers SYN-ACK, acknowledging that start and supplying its own synchronization. The client completes setup with ACK. This is the three-way handshake.

practice.q: Which IPv6 address reaches all routers on the local link?
practice.why: ff02::2 is the IPv6 all-routers multicast group on the local link. ff02::1 is all IPv6 nodes on that link. The group address identifies the intended set of receivers.

practice.q: What does a switch do with unknown unicast traffic?
options: Floods eligible ports in the same VLAN except ingress
practice.why: If the receiver's MAC is unknown, the switch makes copies on eligible forwarding ports in that same VLAN, excluding the arrival port. It does not send those copies across every VLAN.

practice.q: Why is a native VLAN mismatch a problem?
options: Untagged frames can enter different VLANs at the two ends
practice.why: Each trunk end puts untagged frames into its own configured native VLAN. If those settings differ, the same frame can be treated as belonging to different groups at the two ends.

practice.q: A four-member EtherChannel carries one flow. What throughput should you expect?
options: Generally limited by one member link
Always equal to all members combined
practice.why: A conversation is normally assigned to one member link so its packets remain ordered. Several conversations can use different members, increasing total bundle capacity without making one flow use all four links at once.

practice.q: What does BPDU guard do on an edge port receiving a BPDU?
practice.why: A BPDU is a spanning-tree control message. BPDU guard normally puts a protected endpoint port into an error-disabled state when one arrives, because an unexpected switch connection could threaten the intended edge design.

practice.q: Which RSTP state learns MACs but does not forward user frames?
practice.why: In Learning, RSTP can update the switch's MAC-to-port directory but still holds back ordinary user frames. Forwarding is the later state that permits user traffic; Discarding does not perform this learning step.

practice.q: Two protocols offer the same /24. Which preference normally decides installation first?
practice.why: For the identical destination prefix, administrative distance ranks different route sources. Lower is normally preferred. This is separate from choosing the longest matching prefix when forwarding a packet.

practice.q: Which OSPF interface priority makes a router ineligible for DR election?
practice.why: An OSPF interface priority of 0 removes that interface from DR/BDR election eligibility. It can still participate in OSPF; it simply cannot win one of those coordinator roles on that segment.

practice.q: Does a new router with higher priority immediately replace an existing OSPF DR?
practice.why: An established OSPF DR election is nonpreemptive. A new higher-priority router does not immediately take the current DR's role; priority influences an election when the protocol actually needs one.

practice.q: Which IPv6 prefix represents a default route?
practice.why: ::/0 fixes zero destination bits, so it matches every IPv6 destination. It is the default fallback and loses to any more specific installed route that also matches.

practice.q: What allows PAT to distinguish sessions sharing a global IPv4 address?
practice.why: PAT keeps track of address and transport-port mappings, allowing several sessions to share one translated IPv4 address. The port information helps distinguish those conversations; it is not a physical switch-port number.

practice.q: Why is synchronized time useful in network operations?
practice.why: If device clocks agree, operators can compare when related events occurred on different devices. Sending logs to one server does not by itself synchronize the original devices' clocks.

practice.q: What is the correct DHCP message order?
practice.why: Discover looks for DHCP service; Offer proposes settings; Request asks for the selected lease; Acknowledge confirms it. These four stages form the common initial DHCPv4 exchange called DORA.

practice.q: Which notification requests acknowledgment?
practice.why: An SNMP inform asks for an acknowledgment, allowing the sender to know whether its notification was received. A trap sends the notification without that acknowledgment mechanism.

practice.q: Which syslog severity is most serious?
practice.why: Severity 0 means emergency and is the most serious syslog level. Larger numbers are less urgent, ending at 7 for debugging. The scale runs opposite to a higher-is-worse scoring system.

practice.q: Which QoS action normally drops or remarks excess traffic?
practice.why: Policing checks traffic against a rate and normally drops or relabels the excess. Shaping is the alternative that buffers excess packets to transmit later, introducing waiting time.

practice.q: What does a 0 in an ACL wildcard bit mean?
practice.why: A wildcard zero bit means compare this address bit; a one means ignore it. For example, 0.0.0.255 requires the first three address numbers to match and ignores the last number.

practice.q: Which IPv4 standard ACL field is matched?
practice.why: A standard IPv4 ACL checks the sender's source IP address. An extended ACL can also distinguish fields such as destination, protocol and application ports. Attachment and direction still decide where the check applies.

practice.q: DAI normally validates dynamic-host ARP using which information?
practice.why: DHCP snooping records validated client assignments. DAI can compare an ARP claim against that IP-to-MAC binding information; statically addressed devices may need another validated design because no DHCP assignment was learned.

practice.q: Which TCP port is associated with TACACS+?
practice.why: TACACS+ commonly uses TCP 49. RADIUS commonly uses UDP 1812 for authentication and 1813 for accounting. Remember both the transport and number, because a TCP and UDP port are distinct choices.

practice.q: Which wireless approach uses 802.1X/EAP with an authentication server?
practice.why: Enterprise wireless security uses the 802.1X/EAP framework and an authentication service. Personal security uses shared-credential mechanisms such as WPA2 PSK or WPA3 SAE instead.

practice.q: What provides basic routed connectivity for overlay tunnels?
practice.why: The underlay is the real network providing IP reachability between tunnel endpoints. The overlay is logical connectivity built over that transport, so it cannot ignore a broken underlay path.

practice.q: Which HTTP status usually means the caller lacks valid authentication?
practice.why: 401 normally means authentication is missing or invalid. 403 normally means access is forbidden by policy. Check the API documentation and response before treating both as the same failure.

practice.q: Which HTTP method reads a resource?
practice.why: GET asks to read a resource representation. It should not be used to request intended state changes. Other methods express creation, replacement, partial modification or removal according to the API contract.

practice.q: Which is valid JSON?
practice.why: The key uses double quotes and true is an unquoted lowercase boolean. That is valid JSON. Single-quoted keys, trailing commas and undefined are not valid JSON syntax.

practice.q: A /16 must supply equal subnets for at least 500 ordinary usable hosts each. What is the longest suitable prefix?
practice.why: Nine host bits give 2^9 − 2 = 510 ordinary usable addresses, enough for 500. That leaves a /23 prefix. A /24 leaves only eight host bits and 254 usable addresses, which is too small. Inside the original /16, seven bits remain to identify 128 equal /23 subnets.

practice.q: Without NAT or tunneling, what normally changes as a router forwards an IPv4 packet onto another Ethernet link?
options: Destination IP becomes the gateway IP
Layer 2 addresses and TTL change; endpoint IPs remain
The complete incoming frame remains unchanged
practice.why: The router removes the incoming Ethernet wrapper, reduces IPv4 TTL by one and builds the next link's wrapper. The source and destination IP addresses normally remain the same unless another function, such as NAT or tunneling, changes them.

practice.q: A server answers WAN-sourced ping but not LAN-sourced ping from the same router. What should be checked?
options: The remote return route and policy for the LAN prefix
Whether all switches share a MAC
Whether OSPF process IDs equal port numbers
practice.why: A reply is addressed back to the source used in the test. The server may know a route and permit traffic back to the WAN address while lacking that route or permission for the LAN subnet.

practice.q: Two candidate root ports have different total costs to the same root. What is compared first?
practice.why: First compare the total cost of each candidate path toward the root. The lower cost wins. Sender bridge and port identifiers are later tie-breakers, so they do not override an already lower path cost.

practice.q: Correct WLAN and policy profiles exist on a 9800, but the AP carries another policy tag. What should be inspected?
options: The mapping in the policy tag actually applied to that AP
practice.why: On Catalyst 9800, the policy tag actually applied to the AP connects its WLAN with a policy profile. Correct profiles elsewhere do not prove that this AP is using the intended VLAN and rules.

practice.q: Two DROthers are 2-Way with each other and Full with the DR/BDR. What does that indicate?
options: It can be normal broadcast-network behavior
Their local process numbers must match
practice.why: On a broadcast segment, ordinary routers called DROthers normally become Full with the DR/BDR coordinators, but can remain 2-Way with one another. Judge the state against the network type and roles before calling it a fault.

practice.q: What does network 10.1.12.0 0.0.0.255 area 0 primarily select in OSPF configuration?
options: An arbitrary summary regardless of interfaces
Local interfaces matching the address and wildcard
practice.why: The address and wildcard select matching local router interfaces and assign them to area 0. The command does not simply instruct OSPF to advertise an arbitrary remote network that is not selected on a local interface.

practice.q: A dynamic NAT pool has ten global addresses without overload. Eleven inside hosts need simultaneous mappings. What can happen?
options: One cannot obtain a mapping after pool exhaustion
All hosts automatically switch to IPv6
practice.why: Without overload, each simultaneously translated inside address needs its own free pool address. Ten available addresses may leave the eleventh host unable to obtain a mapping until one becomes free or the design changes.

practice.q: How do DSCP and 802.1Q CoS differ?
options: Both are the same six-bit field
DSCP is six-bit IP marking; CoS/PCP is three-bit VLAN-tag marking
DSCP is part of the source MAC
practice.why: DSCP is a six-bit field in the IP header. CoS/PCP is a three-bit field in an 802.1Q VLAN tag. A policy can map CoS 5 to DSCP 46 without making them the same field or encoded number.

practice.q: A broad source-subnet IP permit precedes a TCP 22 deny for that same source. What happens to matching SSH?
options: Rules are sorted by port specificity
practice.why: The packet stops at the first matching entry. The broad permit already matches the SSH packet, so the later TCP 22 deny is never reached. Put the intended specific restriction before the broader allowance.

practice.q: Does DHCP snooping trust automatically enable DAI trust on the same uplink?
options: Yes, there is one shared command
No, DAI has a separate trust setting
practice.why: DHCP snooping trust controls receipt of DHCP server messages. DAI trust controls whether ARP inspection is bypassed. They are separate settings for separate checks; enabling one does not enable the other.

practice.q: After enabling DAI, DHCP clients work but a static server loses ARP connectivity. What may be missing?
options: A validated binding or applicable ARP ACL for the server
An OSPF process matching its VLAN
practice.why: The static server may have no DHCP-learned assignment for DAI to validate. Provide a suitable verified IP-to-MAC binding or ARP ACL instead of declaring every client-facing port trusted.

practice.q: An AI-generated command is unsupported by the target image. What should you do?
options: Validate against the parser, release support and policy
practice.why: A generated command is a proposal. If the actual device does not support it, consult that platform's release documentation and command help, then validate an appropriate alternative. A confident explanation cannot make unsupported syntax work.

practice.q: A request using a valid token receives HTTP 403. What does that normally mean?
options: A missing client route is certain
Forbidden access; inspect permissions and scope
practice.why: 403 normally reports forbidden access under the service's policy, so inspect permissions and token scope. 401 concerns missing or invalid authentication. A token being present does not automatically grant every action.

practice.q: A switch has eight powered ports, but the ninth compatible AP receives no power. The AP works on an unused port of another switch. Which check best follows this evidence?
options: Check the first switch's remaining PoE power budget and port power status.
Replace the wireless controller because it supplies Ethernet power.
Assign the AP a public IPv4 address.
Change the AP's DNS domain before inspecting power.
practice.why: The AP receives power elsewhere, so start with the original port and the switch's remaining power allowance. PoE requires both a compatible port and enough available watts. IP settings cannot turn on an AP that has no power.

practice.q: A company wants malicious traffic blocked before it reaches a server. Which component directly inspects and can stop that traffic while deployed in the forwarding path?
options: A passive packet-capture station with no enforcement link.
A DNS server that only answers name queries.
A patch panel joining two copper cables.
practice.why: Inline means the traffic actually passes through the device. An intrusion prevention system there can inspect and stop matching attacks before delivery. A passive observer can report what it saw but cannot itself drop traffic on that path.

practice.q: A client can ping a server, but its HTTPS connection is refused. Which conclusion is supported?
options: Successful ping proves every server application is working.
An access point must perform the server's TLS handshake.
IP reachability exists, but the HTTPS service or its access policy still needs investigation.
The server must be physically disconnected.
practice.why: Ping and HTTPS test different functions. A successful ping shows IP request/reply reachability for that test; a refused HTTPS connection can still mean the web service is stopped, not listening or rejected by policy.

practice.q: A small campus combines distribution and core functions in one resilient switch pair. What topology does this describe?
options: A single shared coaxial collision domain.
A two-tier campus with a collapsed core.
A three-tier campus with three separate switching layers.
A leaf-spine fabric with no distribution functions.
practice.why: The access layer connects users. Combining distribution and core functions leaves one other functional tier, called a collapsed core. Counting physical boxes or floors does not tell you the number of architectural tiers.

practice.q: A team rents virtual machines and installs and patches the guest operating systems itself. Which cloud service model most closely fits?
options: Software as a Service with no guest OS management.
A physical-only campus with no virtual resources.
A DNS record type that creates virtual machines.
practice.why: In IaaS, the provider supplies infrastructure while the customer normally operates the guest OS and applications. SaaS instead supplies a finished application, and PaaS manages more of the application platform for the customer.

practice.q: In a three-tier campus, access switches connect users and distribution switches apply policy. What is the core layer's main design role?
options: Assign every endpoint its wireless passphrase.
Replace the access layer's endpoint connections.
Store all dynamically learned DNS records.
Provide resilient, fast connectivity between distribution blocks.
practice.why: The core is the reliable, fast connection between distribution areas. User attachments belong at access and aggregation/policy at distribution; separating those jobs helps the larger design scale.

practice.q: Both ends of a fiber link use supported transceivers, but one end is 10G single-mode at 1310 nm and the other is 10G multimode at 850 nm. What must be corrected?
options: Enable TCP acknowledgments on the transceivers.
Use a larger IPv4 subnet to increase optical compatibility.
Match the optical standards and use their supported fiber type.
Set both switch ports to the same native VLAN to match wavelengths.
practice.why: Both ends say 10G, but they use different light wavelengths and fiber standards. Match the supported optical signaling at both ends and install the appropriate fiber; nominal speed and a fitting connector are insufficient.

practice.q: A new access cable must cross an electrically noisy industrial area. Which medium inherently avoids electromagnetic interference in its signal path?
options: Any copper cable after disabling CDP.
Unshielded copper twisted pair because it carries no electrical signal.
A copper console rollover cable used as an Ethernet uplink.
practice.why: Fiber carries light, so electrical noise does not interfere with its data signal as it can with copper's electrical signal. The design still needs suitable distance, optics and installation practices.

practice.q: One end of a legacy Ethernet link is forced to full duplex; the other operates at half duplex. The link is up but performs poorly under load. What is the best repair?
options: Use matching duplex settings, normally compatible autonegotiation at both ends.
Keep the mismatch and increase the OSPF process ID.
Add an unrelated DNS server to remove collisions.
Force a different native VLAN on each end.
practice.why: Half duplex takes turns; full duplex permits simultaneous sending and receiving. Mismatched ends can show an up link yet perform badly. Restore compatible settings, normally supported autonegotiation at both ends, then recheck new error counters.

practice.q: IOS XE reports an Ethernet interface as administratively down, line protocol down. Which fact should be checked before replacing the cable?
options: Whether an OSPF DR has a higher router ID.
Whether the DNS zone contains a CNAME.
Whether a trunk uses the reserved VLAN 4095.
Whether the interface is intentionally shut down in configuration.
practice.why: Administratively down means configuration has disabled the port. First confirm whether shutdown was intended. Use no shutdown only when the design calls for enabling it; replacing the cable does not remove the configured shutdown.

practice.q: A packet capture shows a DHCPv4 client discovery exchange. Which transport and port direction should be expected for the initial client message?
options: UDP from server port 67 toward client port 68 for the client's first message.
TCP port 443 because DHCP always runs over HTTPS.
UDP from client port 68 toward server port 67.
TCP from client port 68 toward server port 67.
practice.why: The initial DHCPv4 client message uses UDP source port 68 and destination port 67. A client without its assigned address can use a broadcast; it does not establish a TCP connection for this exchange.

practice.q: A developer uses UDP for a transaction that still needs lost responses detected. Which design statement is correct?
options: The use of UDP prevents all reliability logic at higher layers.
The application can implement acknowledgments, timeouts and retries above UDP.
UDP will automatically retransmit every missing application response.
UDP guarantees application messages arrive in order.
practice.why: UDP does not track reliable ordered delivery itself. The application can add confirmation messages, wait timers and retries to detect missing responses, choosing the extra overhead and timing behavior it needs.

practice.q: A host is configured as 192.0.2.70/27. Which proposed default gateway is in the same subnet and is an ordinary usable host address?
practice.why: A /27 has 32-address blocks. .70 falls in .64–.95; .64 names the network and .95 is broadcast. Ordinary hosts, including this host's gateway, use .65–.94. Thus .65 fits, while .63 and .97 are outside the block.

practice.q: A VLSM plan already uses 10.20.0.0/25 and 10.20.0.128/26. Which /27 can be added without overlapping either allocation?
practice.why: The existing /25 uses .0–.127 and the existing /26 uses .128–.191. The next free /27 block is .192–.223. A smaller subnet inside either used range would still allocate some of the same addresses twice.

practice.q: A server uses an RFC 1918 address behind a translating gateway. What security conclusion follows from that addressing choice alone?
options: The server no longer needs operating-system updates.
Every Internet router will advertise the server's private subnet.
None of the application access policy is proven; filtering and authentication must still be designed.
All inbound and outbound attacks are automatically prevented.
practice.why: Private addressing controls address allocation and normal public routing, not the complete access policy. It does not encrypt traffic or authenticate users. Decide and verify firewall, login and host protections separately.

practice.q: Two companies both use 10.40.0.0/16 and now want direct routed connectivity between their networks. What issue must the integration plan address?
options: OSPF always combines overlapping companies into a unique public subnet.
Overlapping address space makes destinations ambiguous and needs a deliberate design solution.
RFC 1918 guarantees private prefixes are globally unique.
Changing DNS TTLs automatically makes overlapping routes distinct.
practice.why: Both sites have the same destination block, so ordinary routing cannot tell which identically addressed host is intended. Plan unique addressing or a deliberate translation/isolation solution before joining the networks.

practice.q: An IPv6 host learns an address through SLAAC. Which information normally identifies its default router?
options: The source link-local address of a suitable Router Advertisement.
A DHCPv6 option that is required to carry every IPv6 default gateway.
An IPv4 ARP reply containing an IPv6 broadcast address.
The first public DNS server returned by a query.
practice.why: A suitable Router Advertisement tells the host about a potential default router using the router's link-local source address. DHCPv6 can supply an address or other settings, but it does not replace this default-router discovery role.

practice.q: Two IOS XE router interfaces have valid IPv6 addresses and are up, but IPv6 unicast forwarding between them has not been enabled globally. Which command enables that routing function?
practice.why: ipv6 unicast-routing is the global switch enabling IPv6 packet forwarding between networks. Assigning interface addresses and bringing links up are separate steps and do not automatically enable that global routing function.

practice.q: Using modified EUI-64, what interface identifier is derived from MAC address 00:11:22:33:44:55?
practice.why: 1. Split 00:11:22:33:44:55 in half. 2. Insert ff:fe: 00:11:22:ff:fe:33:44:55. 3. Flip the specified universal/local bit so the first byte changes from 00 to 02. 4. Group pairs of bytes into IPv6 groups: 0211:22ff:fe33:4455. Other interface-ID methods are also common.

practice.q: Several IPv6 service nodes deliberately share the same anycast address. How is a packet to that address normally delivered?
options: Only to the node whose MAC address supplied the address.
To one instance selected by the routing topology.
To every instance through an IPv6 broadcast.
To every instance through mandatory multicast replication.
practice.why: Anycast gives several service instances the same unicast-format address. Routing chooses one reachable instance for a packet. It does not copy that packet to every instance as group delivery would.

practice.q: A site uses fd42:10:20::/48 for internal IPv6 subnets. Which description fits this prefix?
options: Unique local addressing intended for local use, without an expectation of global Internet routing.
Link-local addressing that routers must never forward between local subnets.
A multicast range for all routers on a link.
An IPv4-mapped address that requires NAT44.
practice.why: fd00::/8 is the commonly locally assigned part of fc00::/7 unique-local addressing. These addresses can route between internal subnets; they are not intended for global public routing. Link-local is different because it stays on one link.

practice.q: A Linux host reaches local neighbors but cannot reach any remote subnet. Which command directly displays its default-route selection?
practice.why: ip route show default displays the Linux host's default route. Reaching neighbors on the same subnet does not prove a default gateway exists or works, because those local deliveries do not need it.

practice.q: On macOS, an administrator needs to verify an interface's configured IP address and netmask. Which command is appropriate?
practice.why: ifconfig en0 displays that macOS interface's address, mask and status. Check the actual interface name on the machine; commands for IOS or Windows are not native substitutes for this macOS inspection.

practice.q: Two APs advertise the same SSID. What does matching the SSID alone prove about their encryption settings?
options: Clients are guaranteed seamless authenticated roaming.
Nothing; security settings must be checked independently.
Both APs necessarily share a radio channel.
practice.why: An SSID is only the wireless network name. Two access points can advertise the same name while using different login methods, encryption or VLAN policies. Inspect those settings independently.

practice.q: An administrator increases channel width while keeping the available RF spectrum unchanged. What design trade-off should be considered?
options: Wider channels can improve potential link throughput but leave fewer independent channels for reuse.
Wider channels always create more nonoverlapping channels.
Channel width removes the need to plan neighboring AP channels.
Channel width changes the IPv4 subnet mask of each client.
practice.why: A wider channel occupies more of the available radio spectrum. It may carry more on one good link, but leaves fewer independent channels for nearby access points and can increase competition in a dense network.

practice.q: A server runs several containers and several full virtual machines. Which distinction is normally correct?
options: Every container requires a separate physical CPU.
Full VMs must all share the same guest kernel.
Containers provide physical separation equivalent to separate buildings.
Containers share the host kernel; full VMs can each run their own guest kernel.
practice.why: A full VM can run its own guest operating-system kernel, the core part of that OS. Containers share the host kernel while isolating application processes. Those designs have different resource costs and isolation boundaries.

practice.q: A physical server hosts three virtual machines, each seeing virtual CPUs and memory. Which component allocates those physical resources to the guests?
practice.why: The hypervisor presents virtual hardware and divides real processor, memory and input/output resources among the VMs. A virtual switch handles guest networking instead; it does not allocate the guest processors or memory.

practice.q: A switch receives a frame and finds its destination MAC learned on the same port where the frame arrived, in the same VLAN. What does it normally do?
options: Always transmit it back to the ingress port.
Filter the frame rather than send it back out that same port.
Flood it out all VLANs including unrelated access VLANs.
Route it using an OSPF neighbor table.
practice.why: The switch already knows the receiver is on the segment where the frame arrived. It therefore does not send the frame back out that same port or flood it elsewhere. This differs from having no known receiver entry.

practice.q: A quiet endpoint is moved to a new switch port in the same VLAN. What most directly allows the switch to learn its new location?
options: A received frame carrying that endpoint's source MAC on the new port.
A DNS query that returns the old port number.
The source MAC in a frame transmitted only by a different endpoint.
Changing the endpoint's TCP destination port.
practice.why: The switch learns a device's location when it receives a frame with that device's source MAC on the new port. If the device remains silent, an old entry can remain until its aging timer removes it.

practice.q: VLAN 30 exists on two switches and is allowed across their working trunk. One workstation cannot reach its same-VLAN peer. Which local check best tests whether its access port is in the correct VLAN?
options: Create an OSPF area before checking the access port.
Disable VLAN 30 on the remote switch.
Change the peer to a different VLAN because same-VLAN communication requires routing.
Inspect the port's operational access VLAN with show interfaces switchport.
practice.why: Correct VLANs and a working trunk do not prove that the workstation's own socket belongs to VLAN 30. show interfaces switchport checks that port's operational access VLAN. Same-VLAN peers normally use switching rather than routing.

practice.q: VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 must exchange routed traffic, while VLAN 30 must be isolated from both. All three have SVIs on a Layer 3 switch. Which design meets that requirement?
options: Remove the VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 gateways while leaving VLAN 30 unrestricted.
Use the same access VLAN on all ports and rely on separate subnet names.
Keep the intended routing and apply an explicit filtering policy for VLAN 30, allowing the required VLAN 10-to-20 traffic.
Assume different VLAN numbers automatically block traffic after routing is enabled.
practice.why: VLANs separate local delivery groups, but their working gateways can route between them. Apply deliberate rules to permit Users–Servers and block the required Guest directions, then test both allowed and blocked paths. Any required infrastructure exceptions must be explicit.

practice.q: An IOS XE trunk currently allows VLANs 10 and 20. VLAN 30 must be added while preserving those entries. Which interface command expresses that change?
practice.why: The add keyword extends the existing list while preserving 10 and 20. A list set to only 30 replaces the old list. Changing the native or access VLAN is a different action and does not add VLAN 30 to the allowed set.

practice.q: A port's configuration includes switchport mode trunk, but VLAN 40 traffic does not cross it. Which verification directly checks both operational trunking and VLAN allowance?
practice.why: show interfaces trunk reports actual trunk operation and the relevant allowed, active and forwarding VLAN lists on supported switches. A configuration saying trunk expresses intent; it does not prove VLAN 40 is currently able to cross.

practice.q: LLDP reports an adjacent switch and its connected port. What additional conclusion still requires separate verification?
options: That the devices are physically or logically adjacent on that link.
That the reported port identifier came from a discovery advertisement.
That LLDP can exchange information between different vendors.
Whether an end-to-end application path works across the network.
practice.why: LLDP shows that local discovery messages from the adjacent device were received. It does not test the remote application, the return route, all required VLANs or permission rules along a complete path.

practice.q: Security policy requires CDP disabled on one externally facing interface while retaining it on internal interfaces. Which IOS XE interface command has that scope?
practice.why: In interface mode, no cdp enable turns off CDP only on that selected connection. In global mode, no cdp run turns it off device-wide, which would also remove the intended internal discovery.

practice.q: An IOS XE design uses an LACP EtherChannel as a routed link. Where is the link's Layer 3 address normally configured?
options: On every member using the same connected IP address independently.
On the logical routed Port-channel interface, with compatible routed member interfaces.
On a different access VLAN on each physical member.
Only on the neighbor's loopback, leaving the bundle without addressing.
practice.why: The routed bundle is one logical IP interface. Put its address on Port-channel and keep the physical members compatible and routed. Giving duplicate independent link addresses to members does not create the intended logical bundle.

practice.q: LACP is active at both ends, but a proposed member is suspended after being assigned a different access VLAN from the existing bundle. What should be checked?
options: Consistency of member and Port-channel switching parameters.
Whether both peers can be changed to passive to force negotiation.
Whether the bundle's DNS name is lowercase.
Whether NTP uses TCP instead of UDP.
practice.why: LACP active starts negotiation but does not make incompatible VLAN settings valid. Compare the intended member and Port-channel settings and correct the mismatch before expecting the member to join the bundle.

practice.q: A downstream access switch must never become the STP root through its uplink. Which protection is designed to prevent a superior BPDU on the distribution port from changing the root placement?
options: Disabling all BPDU transmission while leaving redundant links forwarding.
practice.why: Root guard protects the chosen root location. A superior BPDU claims a better route/root than intended, so the protected port can be held root-inconsistent instead of accepting that claim. BPDU guard has a different endpoint-port purpose.

practice.q: A redundant switch link stops receiving expected BPDUs even though the physical link remains up. Which STP protection helps prevent an inappropriate transition to forwarding caused by that loss?
options: DHCP relay on the access VLAN.
An increased DNS TTL for the switch.
Loop guard on appropriate STP ports.
practice.why: Missing expected BPDUs can make a redundant path look safe when it is not. Loop guard can hold the affected port loop-inconsistent rather than let it incorrectly start forwarding. This differs from an edge port receiving an unexpected BPDU.

practice.q: An AP is assigned a dedicated monitoring role for RF observation rather than normal client service. What should users expect?
options: It supplies PoE to its upstream switch.
That AP is not intended to provide ordinary client access while in monitor mode.
It necessarily becomes the default gateway for every client.
It joins every client to an unencrypted SSID.
practice.why: A dedicated monitor-mode AP is assigned to observe the radio environment, not provide ordinary client access. Being powered and visible to management does not change that selected role.

practice.q: A site has autonomous APs with individually maintained WLAN configuration. What operational change is central to adopting a controller-managed architecture?
options: Move supported AP management and WLAN policy coordination into the controller-based workflow.
Require every user packet to pass through the controller CPU in every supported mode.
Eliminate the need for client authentication policy.
Replace all radio channels with VLAN numbers.
practice.why: The controller-based workflow coordinates supported AP configuration and policy instead of maintaining each autonomous AP independently. Follow the architecture to determine the client data path; centralized management alone does not define it.

practice.q: A newly installed lightweight AP has no LEDs and is absent from controller inventory. Which dependency should be verified first?
options: The per-user RADIUS authorization result after association.
The controller's preferred OSPF DR priority.
Its supported power source and physical Ethernet uplink.
practice.why: An unpowered AP cannot run its radios or join a controller. Check its compatible power source, remaining PoE power and cable first, before diagnosing wireless profiles or authentication policy.

practice.q: In a centrally switched WLAN, the AP joins the controller successfully, but the controller's client-VLAN uplink path is broken. What outcome is plausible?
options: Clients must automatically bypass the controller through local switching without configuration.
All wired interfaces are necessarily physically down.
AP management remains visible while client access to that wired VLAN fails.
AP join proves every client VLAN is reachable end to end.
practice.why: The AP's controller-management connection and the client's mapped data connection are separate paths. The AP can remain joined while a broken controller uplink VLAN prevents clients from reaching their gateway or services.

practice.q: A device offers HTTP and HTTPS web management. Which choice protects credentials and page content in transit when properly configured with a validated certificate?
options: Plain TFTP because it is connectionless.
HTTP with a longer browser bookmark name.
practice.why: HTTPS uses TLS to protect the browser session in transit. Validate the device certificate and identity as well as supported settings; ordinary HTTP does not gain encryption from an unrelated configuration change.

practice.q: A management-VLAN configuration error makes a switch unreachable by IP. A technician has authorized local access. Which path can restore CLI access without depending on that IP VLAN?
options: A new SSH session over the same broken management path.
An HTTP request to an unrelated public DNS server.
An SNMP poll sent to the wrong default gateway.
practice.why: A supported console connection does not depend on the production management VLAN's IP reachability. It can provide authorized recovery access with the correct terminal settings and authentication even when that VLAN is misconfigured.

practice.q: An administrator is reviewing a controller GUI that shows both a WLAN profile name and an SSID. Which value identifies the wireless network name a client normally selects?
options: The administrator's profile label in every controller implementation.
practice.why: The SSID is the network name the user normally sees and selects. A WLAN profile name or numeric identifier organizes the controller configuration and may be different from that visible name.

practice.q: After changing a WLAN-to-VLAN mapping in a controller GUI, which evidence best validates the intended operational result?
options: The administrator changes the dashboard color.
The AP model name is visible in inventory.
A test client receives settings from the intended subnet and reaches the permitted gateway/services.
The browser displays a successful Save message, with no client test.
practice.why: A test client shows the policy actually in use: its VLAN/subnet, assigned settings and permitted connections. Saving a controller screen alone may miss a wrong profile assignment or a broken wired path.

practice.q: An IOS XE router has 192.0.2.1/24 configured on an up routed interface. Which routing-table entries normally identify the subnet and the router's own address?
options: Two default routes with the interface MAC address as destination.
A connected 192.0.2.0/24 entry and a local 192.0.2.1/32 entry.
A local 192.0.2.0/24 entry and a connected default route.
Only an OSPF external route to 192.0.2.1/24.
practice.why: The connected /24 describes the attached subnet. The local /32 identifies packets addressed to the router's own 192.0.2.1 interface. The /32 entry does not change the subnet mask used by every host to /32.

practice.q: A route lists next hop 198.51.100.2 and outgoing interface GigabitEthernet0/0. What do those fields represent?
options: The adjacent forwarding target and the local interface used toward it.
The final destination server and its physical switch port.
The router's DNS server and an application socket.
The route's administrative distance and metric.
practice.why: The next hop is the next forwarding target. GigabitEthernet0/0 is this router's own connection used toward it. Neither field is necessarily the final server, and neither is an administrative-distance or cost value.

practice.q: A router receives a packet whose destination matches no installed route, and no default route is present. What is its normal forwarding action?
options: Flood the IP packet out every routed interface.
Create a permanent host route from the packet's source MAC.
Treat the DNS server as an automatic default gateway.
Drop the packet rather than invent a route.
practice.why: The router needs a matching installed route to choose a next step. With none, including no default, it drops the packet rather than guessing or flooding it like an unknown local Ethernet frame. Policy may permit an ICMP error response.

practice.q: OSPF offers two otherwise eligible paths to the same prefix, with costs 20 and 35. Which path is preferred?
options: Both solely because their prefix lengths are equal.
The path received last, regardless of cost.
The path with cost 35 because a higher metric is always preferred.
practice.why: For otherwise comparable OSPF paths to the same prefix, lower cost is better, so 20 beats 35. AD compares different route sources; longest-prefix matching later chooses between installed destination blocks for a packet.

practice.q: An IOS XE router must send destinations not matched by more-specific routes to reachable next hop 192.0.2.2. Which global command creates the required IPv4 static route?
practice.why: The all-zero destination and all-zero mask express 0.0.0.0/0, matching any IPv4 destination. It is used only when no more specific installed route matches. The next hop 192.0.2.2 and the return path still need to work.

practice.q: An IOS XE IPv6 static route uses next-hop address fe80::2. Why must its exit interface also be specified?
options: A link-local address is scoped to its link, so the router needs the interface to identify that link.
Link-local addresses are globally unique Internet destinations.
The interface converts the IPv6 prefix into an IPv4 mask.
Every link-local address is a multicast group that must be flooded.
practice.why: fe80::2 has only local-link scope, and the same written value could exist on more than one link. Naming the exit interface tells the router which link contains the intended neighbor.

practice.q: Two directly connected OSPFv2 routers have unique router IDs and compatible addressing, but one interface is in area 0 and the other in area 1. What must be corrected for their normal neighbor relationship?
options: Make their locally significant process IDs equal while keeping the area mismatch.
Give both routers the same router ID.
Disable the physical link to force a DR election.
Put the connected OSPF interfaces in the same intended area.
practice.why: OSPF neighbors on the shared connection must agree on their area. Correct the intended interfaces to the same area and check the other neighbor requirements. Their local process numbers may differ, while their router IDs should be unique.

practice.q: An OSPFv2 process starts with no explicit router-id. It has loopback addresses 10.0.0.9 and 10.0.0.2 and an active physical address 203.0.113.254. Which router ID is normally selected?
options: 0.0.0.0 because private addresses cannot be router IDs.
practice.why: With no configured router ID, eligible loopbacks are considered before physical interfaces. Of 10.0.0.9 and 10.0.0.2, .9 is higher, so it wins. Selection occurs when the process chooses its ID; a later address change need not replace an active ID.

practice.q: Two OSPFv2 neighbors consistently stall in Exstart/Exchange. Area, timers and authentication match, but the interfaces use different IP MTUs. Which check best follows?
options: Enable PortFast on the router process.
Compare and reconcile the intended MTU settings and link support.
Change the DNS suffix to match the OSPF process ID.
Assume the adjacency is fully established because Hello packets are present.
practice.why: MTU is the maximum IP packet size supported on the link. Mismatched values can stop the routers exchanging their OSPF database descriptions even though initial neighbor messages work. Check and reconcile the intended actual link support.

practice.q: A working FHRP gateway fails over to its standby router. What allows hosts to continue using the same default-gateway configuration?
options: The virtual gateway identity is taken over by the surviving router.
Every host must be manually assigned the standby's physical interface address.
The hosts automatically convert to Layer 2 switching between all subnets.
DNS replaces the default route with an AP's BSSID.
practice.why: The surviving router takes over the shared virtual gateway identity. Hosts continue using the same virtual IP rather than being reconfigured to the survivor's physical address. The protocol's virtual-MAC and takeover mechanisms support local delivery.

practice.q: An active gateway's LAN interface remains up, but its only upstream path fails. Why might a basic FHRP setup fail to restore off-subnet access by itself?
options: FHRP always tests every application on every remote subnet.
A virtual IP guarantees that all upstream routes are valid.
A standby gateway must be in a different host subnet.
Gateway-role availability alone does not necessarily track usable upstream reachability.
practice.why: The client can still reach its gateway while the gateway cannot reach anything beyond it. A basic role election may not notice that remote failure. Coordinate upstream routing and supported tracking with failover so the chosen gateway has a useful path.

practice.q: A static mapping translates inside host 10.30.0.10 to 198.51.100.10 for outside use. In NAT terminology, what is 10.30.0.10?
options: The outside global address of every Internet client.
practice.why: Inside local means the inside host's address as used internally, so it is 10.30.0.10. Inside global is its translated outside identity, 198.51.100.10. The terms describe viewpoints, not which side of a drawing the router is on.

practice.q: An ACL is referenced by an IOS XE inside-source NAT rule but is not applied to an interface as a traffic filter. What does a permit in that NAT selection ACL normally identify?
options: A guarantee that the outside destination will reply.
Traffic eligible for that translation rule.
Traffic universally authorized through every firewall.
A packet that must be dropped before routing.
practice.why: Here the ACL is a selector for the NAT rule: permit means eligible for translation. It has not been attached as an interface traffic filter, so it does not alone create the network's complete security policy.

practice.q: A switch synchronizes directly to a valid stratum-2 NTP server. What stratum does the synchronized switch normally advertise to its own clients?
options: Stratum 2 regardless of the synchronization chain.
practice.why: A synchronized client is normally one hierarchy step beyond its chosen server. Server stratum 2 plus one gives client stratum 3. The number describes the time-source hierarchy; it does not guarantee clock accuracy or low delay. Stratum 16 means unsynchronized.

practice.q: An administrator adds ntp server 192.0.2.10 on IOS XE. What evidence is still needed before treating the clock as synchronized?
options: Verify that the server address contains four octets.
Confirm that Telnet is enabled on every VTY line.
Assume the command instantly synchronizes time even if UDP is filtered.
Verify a selected association and synchronized status, not just the presence of the configuration line.
practice.why: The configured server line names an intended source. show ntp associations and show ntp status help confirm that a source was actually selected and synchronization occurred. Check reachability and matching authentication if that has not happened.

practice.q: A service name should be an alias for another DNS name rather than directly storing its IPv4 or IPv6 address. Which record type is appropriate?
practice.why: CNAME points one DNS name to another name. A and AAAA store IP addresses directly, while PTR supports reverse address-to-name lookup. Choose the record matching the relationship you need.

practice.q: A DHCPv4 client has received an OFFER and sent a REQUEST for the offered lease. Which message normally confirms the server's assignment?
practice.why: An OFFER is a proposal. After the client REQUEST, the server's DHCPACK normally confirms the lease and its settings. Receiving only a proposal is not evidence that the entire assignment succeeded.

practice.q: A monitoring system regularly sends SNMP GET requests for an interface counter. Which role does the router's SNMP process perform?
options: Agent, exposing managed objects for the manager to query.
Manager, because every queried device is the manager.
Authoritative DNS server for the counter OID.
An NTP reference clock because it responds periodically.
practice.why: The monitoring system is the manager asking for a value. The router's agent exposes the managed counter and answers. An OID names that value; it is not a destination route for forwarding user packets.

practice.q: A monitoring account only needs to retrieve counters. Which authorization is most appropriate?
options: Unrestricted write access to all configuration objects.
No authentication because a read operation cannot reveal information.
Permission to create any local privileged user.
A read-only view limited to the required management objects.
practice.why: Reading counters does not require permission to alter configuration. A limited read-only view supplies the needed information while reducing authority. Authentication, encryption and which objects may be read are separate settings.

practice.q: In a Cisco-style syslog identifier such as %LINK-3-UPDOWN, what does LINK identify?
options: The severity number 3 written in another format.
practice.why: In %LINK-3-UPDOWN, LINK names the subsystem producing the message, 3 is the severity and UPDOWN is the event shorthand. LINK is not the log server's address or the threshold setting.

practice.q: Two devices log related failures using unsynchronized clocks. What is the operational consequence even if both send messages to the same collector?
options: UDP changes every device's clock to the collector time.
The apparent event order can be misleading unless clock and timestamp information are accounted for.
The collector automatically proves the devices' actual event times were identical.
practice.why: One collector can receive messages from clocks that disagree. Their original timestamps can therefore imply the wrong event order. Synchronize sources and account for time zones and collection delay before drawing that conclusion.

practice.q: A DHCPv4 server serves several remote client subnets through relay agents. Which relay information normally helps it choose the correct client subnet pool?
options: The relay agent address in giaddr.
The client's HTTPS certificate common name.
The OSPF DR priority of the DNS server.
practice.why: The relay's giaddr field provides subnet context for the remote server to choose a suitable client pool. The server also needs a valid route back to the relay; pool selection alone does not deliver the reply.

practice.q: An IOS XE router's WAN interface should obtain its IPv4 address from an upstream DHCP server. Which interface command configures that client behavior?
practice.why: ip address dhcp makes the selected interface request its own address. ip helper-address forwards other clients' requests, while ip dhcp pool defines server settings. Client, relay and server are different jobs.

practice.q: A QoS policy identifies voice packets by traffic characteristics, then sets their DSCP value. What are these two operations, in order?
practice.why: Classification identifies the traffic group first. Marking then writes a label such as DSCP. A label alone neither reserves bandwidth nor proves that later devices apply the intended treatment.

practice.q: Voice is assigned a strict-priority queue on a congested link. Why should the policy control the priority class's admitted or transmitted rate?
options: A voice packet can never be incorrectly classified.
Unbounded priority traffic could starve other queues.
Strict priority automatically increases the physical link speed.
Priority queuing removes all serialization delay.
practice.why: Strict priority serves that queue ahead of others. If too much traffic qualifies without limits, other queues can be starved. Bound and classify priority traffic carefully; the physical link still has finite capacity.

practice.q: An IOS XE lab router already has working SSH keys and IP reachability. A local user exists, but the VTY lines still use only a shared line password. Which VTY command selects local-user authentication in a non-AAA configuration?
practice.why: In this non-AAA example, login local tells the VTY lines to check the device's local username database. SSH keys and encrypted transport do not automatically select that database for authentication.

practice.q: An SSH client reports a changed host key for a router. What is the appropriate response before submitting credentials?
options: Always accept the new key because encryption proves the peer is legitimate.
Send the password over Telnet to test it.
Disable host-key checking permanently on all management clients.
Verify the router's identity and key change through a trusted channel.
practice.why: The host key helps identify the server, separately from the user's password. A changed key could be an authorized replacement or an impersonator/wrong target. Verify it through an independent trusted route before accepting it or submitting credentials.

practice.q: A firewall allows an FTP client's TCP control session to server port 21, but directory listings and transfers fail. Which dependency must also be examined?
options: An OSPF neighbor relationship between the FTP applications.
A DHCP relay that turns FTP into UDP.
The separate FTP data connection and its active/passive-mode firewall/NAT handling.
An NTP multicast group carrying the file bytes.
practice.why: TCP 21 carries FTP control commands, but file data and directory listings need a separate data connection. Active and passive modes use different directions/ports, so firewall and NAT handling must support the actual selected mode.

practice.q: A backup crosses an untrusted network using ordinary FTP with no TLS or other protective tunnel. What property must the administrator account for?
options: A successful transfer proves the network cannot observe its content.
The session does not provide encrypted confidentiality for its credentials and content.
FTP automatically encrypts credentials whenever TCP is used.
FTP uses SSH host keys because it is identical to SFTP.
practice.why: Ordinary FTP sends credentials and content without encrypted confidentiality. TCP can deliver data reliably without hiding it. Protected alternatives such as FTPS or SFTP are distinct protocols/workflows, not encryption automatically added by TCP.

practice.q: A branch router has a known software weakness, and an exposed service makes exploitation plausible. Which statement correctly distinguishes the terms?
options: The weakness is a vulnerability; a potential exploit is a threat, and risk considers likelihood and impact.
The weakness is automatically an authorized user.
Risk means only the hardware purchase price, regardless of likelihood.
A vulnerability proves that an attacker has already exploited the router.
practice.why: The software weakness is the vulnerability. A possible harmful exploitation is a threat; risk considers its likelihood and consequences. That possibility does not prove an attack already happened, so investigate evidence as well as exposure.

practice.q: A firewall blocks a vulnerable service from untrusted networks, but the underlying software remains unpatched. How should the result be described?
options: The firewall has rewritten the vulnerable source code.
Every possible attack path has been eliminated permanently.
The router no longer requires authenticated administration.
Exposure is reduced, but the vulnerability still exists and needs appropriate remediation.
practice.why: The firewall reduces who can reach the vulnerable service, but the software defect remains. That is mitigation of exposure rather than removal of the flaw. Plan patching and verification alongside the filtering control.

practice.q: An employee holds a secured equipment-room door open for an unknown person who presents no badge. Which security issue does this illustrate?
options: A valid second authentication factor for the visitor.
A DNS cache that is too small.
Tailgating that bypasses individual physical access verification.
practice.why: The unknown person bypasses the individual badge check by following someone else through. That is tailgating. Follow the approved visitor-verification process rather than treating proximity to an authorized employee as permission.

practice.q: Public visitors can enter an office lobby containing an exposed network switch. Which improvement directly reduces unauthorized physical access to its ports and console?
options: Publish the console password on a label next to the switch.
Place the equipment in an appropriately secured enclosure with controlled access.
Increase the DNS TTL on the switch hostname.
practice.why: A controlled enclosure prevents casual physical access to cable ports and the console. Logical login and network controls remain useful, but they do not physically stop a visitor unplugging or connecting equipment.

practice.q: A local username authenticates an administrator to user EXEC, while a separate secret is intended to control entry to privileged EXEC. Which IOS XE setting serves that latter purpose?
practice.why: enable secret protects the transition into privileged EXEC when that path is used. The local username handles login identity instead. Use a supported strong secret type; reversible password disguises are not equivalent protection.

practice.q: A standalone IOS XE lab uses no AAA configuration. A local username and secret are defined, but the console line has no authentication selection. What line command selects the local user database?
practice.why: login local under the console selects the existing local account database in this non-AAA lab. Defining a user does not automatically choose that database for every access line. Preserve a tested authorized recovery path when changing login behavior.

practice.q: A leaked password from an unrelated site is tried against a network administrator's account. Which practice most directly reduces the chance that the same leaked password succeeds?
options: Store the password in an unencrypted public configuration backup.
Disable authentication whenever access is from an RFC 1918 address.
Use a unique strong password for the administrator account, supported by a password manager and MFA where available.
Reuse one password everywhere but change the username capitalization.
practice.why: A unique administrator password means a leak from another website does not expose the same reused secret. A password manager helps maintain uniqueness, while MFA adds another control rather than replacing good secret handling.

practice.q: An authentication system validates a client certificate and requires proof that the client holds its private key. Which authentication principle does that proof use?
options: A guarantee that every user of the device is automatically authorized for all commands.
Possession of the private key corresponding to the certificate.
Knowledge of the public certificate alone, which must remain secret.
The number of routers in the forwarding path.
practice.why: The public certificate names a public key and is not secret. Proving possession of the matching private key supplies the identity evidence. That proof does not automatically authorize every subsequent action.

practice.q: An IPsec site-to-site tunnel protects traffic between its gateways. Which statement correctly describes that protection's limits?
options: Tunnel protection does not by itself prove that either endpoint application or internal host is uncompromised.
IPsec replaces application authentication and host updates.
An encrypted tunnel means malicious content cannot pass through it.
All traffic generated anywhere in either site is always included regardless of policy.
practice.why: IPsec protects selected packets while traveling between the VPN endpoints. It does not prove that a computer is uninfected or an application trustworthy. Routes and selectors also decide which packets actually enter that protection.

practice.q: A traveling employee uses a VPN client on a laptop to securely reach the company network. Which VPN model does this describe?
options: A site-to-site tunnel that requires a gateway router at both offices.
A Layer 2 VLAN trunk that must cross every Internet router.
practice.why: The employee's individual laptop connects through a VPN client, so this is remote access. Site-to-site instead connects networks through gateways. A working VPN still grants only the resource access allowed by policy.

practice.q: Packets from client subnet A enter a router on GigabitEthernet0/0 and leave toward a server on GigabitEthernet0/1. Where does an ACL applied inbound on GigabitEthernet0/0 inspect those packets?
options: Only when returning from the server on the opposite interface.
On every interface in both directions automatically.
As they enter the router from subnet A, before forwarding toward the server.
practice.why: Inbound means entering this router through the selected interface. The ACL checks packets arriving from subnet A on g0/0 before they are forwarded toward the server. Direction is relative to the interface, not a user's idea of upload or download.

practice.q: An administrator creates an IPv4 extended ACL with the intended deny and permit entries. Transit traffic is unchanged. Which missing step should be checked first?
options: Whether all ports are changed into the same VLAN.
Whether the ACL is applied to the intended interface and direction or other relevant feature.
Whether the ACL name contains an OSPF area number.
Whether the DNS cache contains every denied source address.
